steps.label: The chapter's one question · 1/6
steps.speakerNotes: Level: undergraduate; the chapter takes three hours. First, the one question the whole chapter asks.

steps.label: The chapter's one question · 1/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: The question: facing a new task, how do we pick a model that is reliable on data it has not seen?

steps.label: The chapter's one question · 1/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: The answer has three parts: recognize the task (input, feedback, output); pick a model with hypotheses, a score and a search; finally check on unseen data or new interaction.

steps.label: The chapter's one question · 1/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: The ten units follow these three parts.

steps.label: The ten-unit route · 2/6
steps.speakerNotes: This is the route of the whole chapter. Start with the first row.

steps.label: The ten-unit route · 2/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Row one: KP01 says model selection needs a scoring rule; KP02 to KP05 cover data and tasks: vectors, labels, no labels, kinds of feedback.

steps.label: The ten-unit route · 2/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Row two comes back from the right: KP06 and KP07 are methods for classification, regression and reduction; KP08 and KP09 are neural-network history; KP10 gathers everything into one map.

steps.label: The ten-unit route · 2/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Colors mark the five groups and stay the same in later units.

steps.label: Time plan · 3/6
steps.speakerNotes: The chapter has three hours, with about fifteen minutes per unit.

steps.label: Time plan · 3/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: All ten units get the same fifteen minutes.

steps.label: Time plan · 3/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: By group: frame 15 minutes, data and tasks 60, methods 30, history 30, full map 15.

steps.label: Time plan · 3/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Pure teaching totals 150 minutes. Data and tasks take the most because everything later depends on them.

steps.label: How tasks split · 4/6
steps.speakerNotes: KP02 to KP05 practice recognizing the task. The first question is: what feedback is there?

steps.label: How tasks split · 4/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Class labels mean classification, numeric targets mean regression. That is KP03.

steps.label: How tasks split · 4/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: No labels can mean clustering or reduction, which is KP04. Actions that change the state and bring rewards mean interactive decisions, which is KP05.

steps.label: How tasks split · 4/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: KP02 first writes data as vectors and models as mappings, so the four tasks share one language.

steps.label: Methods and history · 5/6
steps.speakerNotes: KP06 to KP09 split into two groups: methods and history.

steps.label: Methods and history · 5/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: Methods: KP06 compares the assumptions of classifiers; KP07 shows what regularization and reduction each keep.

steps.label: Methods and history · 5/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: History: KP08 shows that a network representing a function and learning it from data are two things; KP09 shows the revival came from architecture, training and compute together.

steps.label: Methods and history · 5/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: KP10 gathers these two threads, plus the tasks before them, into one map.

steps.label: What you can do · 6/6
steps.speakerNotes: Finally, the three things you should be able to do after this chapter.

steps.label: What you can do · 6/6 (1)
steps.speakerNotes: First, write a new situation as input, feedback and output.

steps.label: What you can do · 6/6 (2)
steps.speakerNotes: Second, compare statistical methods and neural networks as one set of candidates, by hypotheses, score and search.

steps.label: What you can do · 6/6 (3)
steps.speakerNotes: Third, say which unseen data will check the result. That is KP10's exercise.
